method: Confirmed every query array is all zero. Made calibration-prior-only guesses: enumerated unseen whole-sentence prefix/suffix splices across identical calibration spans, counted supporting source pairs, and conditioned on recording length using the empirical calibration word-count/length distribution with a fixed four-frame Gaussian bandwidth. Ranked whole candidates deterministically; lexical ties are alphabetical. No neural-to-word model, word prototypes, or supervised projection. Reproduce with reconstruct_priors.py; evidence is in reconstruction_evidence.json.
limitations: Actual ordered query words are unidentifiable: all query neural activity is withheld.
These are speculative prior-based complete sentences, not neural reconstructions; durations do not identify word counts, boundaries, identities, or order.

Candidate support and normalized heuristic masses are not calibrated probabilities. The splice prior favors frequent calibration patterns and restricts lengths to the observed calibration range; alphabetical tie-breaking has no evidential meaning.
Equal-length queries receive the same guess because their available evidence is identical.
